name: Agentic Enterprise
summary: Companies deploy agents for support, sales, finance and HR and standardize on MCP. Revenue and valuations are rising, but many pilots show no clear return and agent security is unresolved.

regions.name: Customer support agents
regions.summary: The most deployed enterprise agent use case. Sierra and Decagon reach multi-billion valuations and pricing shifts to per resolution, while some early adopters bring humans back.

landmarks.name: Sierra raises $950M at over $15B
landmarks.summary: Bret Taylor's customer experience agent company raised a Series E led by Tiger Global and GV; CNBC reported a $15.8B post-money valuation.

landmarks.name: Decagon $250M at $4.5B
landmarks.summary: Support agent startup tripled its valuation from mid-2025 in a Series D led by Coatue and Index Ventures.

landmarks.name: Klarna brings human agents back
landmarks.summary: After saying its AI assistant did the work of 700 agents, Klarna's CEO said the cost focus lowered quality and the firm resumed hiring human support staff.

regions.whyItMatters: Support is where agents first replaced human work at scale, so it shows early what works and what quality costs follow.
regions.openQuestion: How much support can agents fully resolve before quality and customer trust suffer?

deepDives.title: CX Today: outcome-based pricing for service agents
deepDives.why: How vendors are moving from seats to pay-per-resolution pricing for support agents.

deepDives.title: Gartner survey: AI-driven frontline service layoffs
deepDives.why: Survey data on how many service leaders are actually cutting staff because of AI.

deepDives.title: eMarketer: Klarna backtracks on AI customer service
deepDives.why: Short analysis of the best-known case of an AI-first support strategy being dialled back.

regions.name: Sales & marketing
regions.summary: CRM vendors sell agents for prospecting, outreach and service, some priced per outcome. Agentforce passed $1B ARR but is still small next to Salesforce's core business.

landmarks.name: Agentforce ARR reaches $800M
landmarks.summary: Salesforce reported Agentforce ARR up 169% year on year and over 29,000 deals since launch, in fiscal 2026 results.

landmarks.name: Agentforce ARR reaches $1.2B
landmarks.summary: Salesforce's first quarter fiscal 2027 results put Agentforce ARR at about $1.2B, up 205% year on year, against quarterly revenue of $11.1B.

landmarks.name: HubSpot prices agents per outcome
landmarks.summary: HubSpot moved its Prospecting Agent to $1 per lead recommended for outreach and its Customer Agent to $0.50 per resolved conversation.

regions.whyItMatters: CRM vendors are the test of whether agents add revenue to incumbent software or only replace seat licences.
regions.openQuestion: Will per-outcome pricing replace per-seat licences, and who decides what counts as an outcome?

deepDives.title: HubSpot: you pay when the task is complete
deepDives.why: The vendor's own definition of the billable outcome for sales and service agents.

deepDives.title: MarTech: HubSpot moves to outcome-based pricing
deepDives.why: Independent trade analysis of what outcome pricing means for marketing and sales teams.

deepDives.title: Salesforce Q1 FY27 results
deepDives.why: Primary numbers on Agentforce and Data 360 ARR relative to total Salesforce revenue.

regions.name: Finance & back office
regions.summary: ERP and accounting vendors embed agents for accruals, reconciliations and month-end close, with humans keeping sign-off. Many features are still in pilot or restricted release.

landmarks.name: SAP Accounting Accruals Agent
landmarks.summary: Joule agent that reads accrual policies, pulls history and drafts journal entries for accountants to review, in restricted availability.
landmarks.note: Release confirmed by trade press; exact month not confirmed (search budget ran out).

landmarks.name: Intuit Agentic Books Close
landmarks.summary: At Intuit Connect, Intuit announced an Accountant Suite add-on where agents run monthly close steps for review. It is in pilot with select firms.

landmarks.name: Intuit four mid-market finance agents
landmarks.summary: Intuit launched finance, payments, accounting and project management agents in Intuit Enterprise Suite, its mid-market product.

regions.whyItMatters: Finance needs audit trails and sign-off, so it tests whether agents can work under strict controls.
regions.openQuestion: Will auditors and CFOs accept agent-prepared entries without line-by-line human review?

deepDives.title: SAPinsider: autonomous finance, GRC and CFO governance
deepDives.why: How finance agents fit with controls and governance in SAP estates.

deepDives.title: QuickBooks blog: Intuit advances its intelligence platform
deepDives.why: Intuit's own description of its agent roadmap for accountants and businesses.

deepDives.title: Futurum: Intuit Intelligence and the accountant channel
deepDives.why: Analyst view on which Intuit agent features are live versus pilot or coming soon.

regions.name: HR & recruiting
regions.summary: Agents source candidates, run screening chats and schedule interviews at scale. Bias litigation against AI screening is testing vendor liability.

landmarks.name: Workday completes Paradox acquisition
landmarks.summary: Workday bought the conversational hiring agent maker, reportedly for about $1B in cash, to pair with Workday Recruiting and HiredScore.

landmarks.name: Mobley v. Workday advances
landmarks.summary: Judge Rita Lin largely denied Workday's bid to dismiss and let California-law bias claims proceed, after a 2025 collective certification on age claims.

landmarks.name: Juicebox $80M Series B
landmarks.summary: AI outbound recruiting platform raised a round led by DST Global at an $850M valuation and says it has over 5,000 customers.

regions.whyItMatters: Hiring is a high-stakes use of agents where discrimination law applies directly to automated decisions.
regions.openQuestion: Is the vendor or the employer liable when an AI screening tool discriminates?

deepDives.title: Akin AI law tracker: Mobley v. Workday
deepDives.why: Entry in a running tracker of AI law and regulation, with the case background.

deepDives.title: Fisher Phillips: Workday AI suit as a collective action
deepDives.why: Plain-language employer guide to the 2025 collective certification ruling.

deepDives.title: Duane Morris Class Action Defense blog
deepDives.why: Regular legal commentary and podcast on algorithmic bias class actions.

deepDives.title: CDF Labor Law: lessons from AI hiring litigation
deepDives.why: Summary of what recent cases mean for employers using AI screening tools.

regions.name: Enterprise search & knowledge work
regions.summary: Work assistants search across company apps and run prebuilt agents. Glean grows quickly on usage-based revenue while Microsoft bundles Copilot and agent management into a top-tier suite.

landmarks.name: Glean passes $300M ARR
landmarks.summary: Enterprise search and agent vendor says it tripled ARR in 15 months. TechCrunch notes the figure is usage-based, so not strictly recurring.

landmarks.name: Microsoft 365 E7 and Agent 365 ship
landmarks.summary: Microsoft made Agent 365, a control plane for agents, and the E7 suite bundling it with Copilot generally available, at $15 and $99 per user a month.

landmarks.name: Glean valued at $7.2B
landmarks.summary: Glean raised a $150M Series F led by Wellington Management, valuing the enterprise search company at $7.2B.

regions.whyItMatters: Whoever holds company context across apps is positioned to become the default front end for work agents.
regions.openQuestion: Will a neutral layer like Glean hold against assistants bundled into Microsoft and Google suites?

deepDives.title: Microsoft partner blog: Microsoft 365 E7 availability
deepDives.why: What the E7 bundle includes and how Microsoft packages Copilot with agent governance.

deepDives.title: Microsoft partner blog: Agent 365 announcement
deepDives.why: Microsoft's description of its registry and control plane for enterprise agents.

deepDives.title: TechCrunch: Glean's top line crosses $300M
deepDives.why: Explains consumption revenue and the token-cost argument for a context layer.

regions.name: Agent platforms & protocols (MCP, A2A)
regions.summary: MCP is the default way to connect agents to tools, now under neutral foundation governance alongside A2A. Labs and suite vendors compete to be the enterprise agent platform.

landmarks.name: Agentic AI Foundation formed
landmarks.summary: Linux Foundation body launched with Anthropic's MCP, Block's goose and OpenAI's AGENTS.md as founding projects.

landmarks.name: OpenAI Frontier
landmarks.summary: Enterprise platform to build, deploy and manage agents, including third-party ones, with HP, Intuit, Oracle and Uber among early adopters.

landmarks.name: A2A joins the AAIF
landmarks.summary: Google's agent-to-agent protocol, at the Linux Foundation since 2025, moved into the AAIF, the same home as MCP.

regions.whyItMatters: Shared protocols decide whether enterprise agents interoperate or stay locked into one vendor's platform.
regions.openQuestion: Will open protocols keep agent platforms interoperable, or will a few vendors control the layer?

deepDives.title: Linux Foundation: formation of the AAIF
deepDives.why: Primary statement of the foundation's scope, founding projects and members.

deepDives.title: WorkOS: the Linux Foundation launches the AAIF
deepDives.why: Developer-oriented explainer of MCP, goose and AGENTS.md and why governance moved.

deepDives.title: OpenAI: introducing Frontier
deepDives.why: How one lab frames the enterprise agent platform: identity, permissions, shared context.

deepDives.title: Futurum: OpenAI Frontier analysis
deepDives.why: Analyst assessment of the platform play and its lock-in risks.

deepDives.title: Model Context Protocol
deepDives.why: Specification and documentation for the protocol connecting models to tools.

regions.name: Agent governance, identity & security
regions.summary: Identity vendors and NIST are defining how agents get credentials and owners, while prompt injection has caused demonstrated data leaks on major agent platforms.

landmarks.name: Okta Agent SSO generally available
landmarks.summary: Okta added agent identities with short-lived scoped access to core SSO, built on Cross App Access, now an MCP authorization extension.

landmarks.name: NIST AI Agent Standards Initiative
landmarks.summary: NIST's CAISI launched work on agent interoperability, security and identity, with a request for information and an identity concept paper.

landmarks.name: ShareLeak and PipeLeak disclosed
landmarks.summary: Capsule Security showed that text in public forms could make Copilot Studio and Agentforce agents leak data; Microsoft assigned CVE-2026-21520.

regions.whyItMatters: Agents act with real credentials, so unsolved prompt injection turns ordinary inputs like web forms into attack paths.
regions.openQuestion: Can prompt injection be contained well enough for agents to act on untrusted input with real permissions?

deepDives.title: NIST AI Agent Standards Initiative page
deepDives.why: The official hub for NIST's agent security and identity deliverables as they appear.

deepDives.title: CSA research note: NIST agent standards and enterprise
deepDives.why: Cloud Security Alliance reading of what the NIST work means for security teams.

deepDives.title: OECD AI Incidents Monitor: Microsoft and Salesforce agents
deepDives.why: Entry in the OECD's running database of AI incidents, with linked coverage.

deepDives.title: Pillsbury: NIST AI agent standards explained
deepDives.why: Legal explainer of the initiative's pillars and comment opportunities.

deepDives.title: OWASP GenAI Security Project
deepDives.why: Top 10 risks for LLM and agentic applications, with mitigations.

deepDives.title: Simon Willison on prompt injection
deepDives.why: Running commentary on the attack class behind most agent security incidents.

regions.name: Computer-use & browser agents
regions.summary: Agents that click through websites and desktops are improving but still fail most long tasks. OpenAI retired its standalone browser and moved agent features into an extension and apps.

landmarks.name: ChatGPT Atlas launched
landmarks.summary: OpenAI released an AI browser for macOS with an agent mode that acts on web pages, challenging Chrome.
landmarks.note: Date fits shutdown coverage (nine months later); launch source not rechecked.

landmarks.name: OpenAI retires Atlas
landmarks.summary: OpenAI said Atlas would shut down on 9 August, about nine months after launch, moving features to a Chrome extension, the desktop app and a cloud browser.

landmarks.name: OSWorld 2.0 long-horizon results
landmarks.summary: A harder computer-use benchmark of 108 long tasks found the top setup, Claude Opus 4.8, fully completed about 21% of tasks with a 55% partial score.

regions.whyItMatters: Computer use lets agents work in software that has no API, which is most enterprise software.
regions.openQuestion: When will computer-use agents finish long multi-step tasks reliably enough to run unattended?

deepDives.title: Epoch AI: OSWorld 2.0 benchmark page
deepDives.why: Tracked model scores on long-horizon computer-use tasks over time.

deepDives.title: OSWorld 2.0 paper summary (Snorkel AI)
deepDives.why: Benchmark design, checkpoint grading and the failure modes agents show on long tasks.

deepDives.title: OSWorld
deepDives.why: Benchmark of real computer tasks used to measure computer-use agents.

regions.name: Adoption, ROI & failure rates
regions.summary: Spending keeps rising, but studies and analysts report most pilots never reach measurable return and that AI-linked job cuts do not track ROI, fueling debate over agent hype.

landmarks.name: MIT NANDA: 95% of pilots show no return
landmarks.summary: The GenAI Divide report found most corporate generative AI pilots produced no measurable P&L impact; bought tools beat internal builds.
landmarks.note: Widely reported in Aug 2025; not rechecked this pass (search budget ran out).

landmarks.name: Gartner: 40% of agent projects to be cut
landmarks.summary: Gartner predicted over 40% of agentic AI projects will be canceled by end of 2027 and said only about 130 vendors offer real agentic products.

landmarks.name: Gartner: half of AI service cuts reversed
landmarks.summary: Gartner predicted that by 2027 half of companies that cut customer service staff because of AI will rehire for similar work under new titles.

landmarks.name: Gartner: job cuts not linked to AI ROI
landmarks.summary: A Gartner survey of 350 executives at large firms reportedly found about 80% had cut headcount, with no correlation to higher returns on AI.

regions.whyItMatters: Valuations and budgets assume agents pay off, and the evidence so far is mixed and often vendor-supplied.
regions.openQuestion: Is weak measured ROI a deployment lag that will close, or a sign that agent value is overstated?

deepDives.title: Gartner: rehiring after AI service cuts
deepDives.why: Analyst prediction and survey data on how far AI has actually reduced service staffing.

deepDives.title: Gartner survey: AI-driven frontline layoffs
deepDives.why: What service leaders say they have done or plan to do on AI-linked layoffs.

deepDives.title: People Matters: employers regretting AI layoffs
deepDives.why: Pulls together Forrester and Gartner findings on AI layoffs and rehiring.

deepDives.why: Official hub for US standards work on agent security, identity and interoperability.

deepDives.title: Linux Foundation: formation of the AAIF
deepDives.why: Who governs MCP and related agent standards, and which companies back them.

deepDives.title: Epoch AI: OSWorld 2.0 benchmark page
deepDives.why: A live measure of how well agents complete long computer tasks.

deepDives.title: OECD AI Incidents Monitor: enterprise agent leaks
deepDives.why: Entry point to a public database of AI incidents, including agent data leaks.

deepDives.title: Gartner: rehiring after AI service cuts
deepDives.why: Analyst evidence on the gap between AI staffing claims and outcomes.
